questions.q: What is unusual about Oracle's DATE type compared to the other platforms in this lesson?
options: It always includes a time component down to the second, unlike a true date-only type
It is identical to SQL Server's DATETIMEOFFSET, including timezone awareness
Oracle has no DATE type at all, only TIMESTAMP
It cannot store any date before the year 2000
questions.explain: Oracle's DATE always carries a time component to the second, which surprises developers expecting date-only storage.

questions.q: What is the real, documented gotcha with MySQL's TIMESTAMP compared to DATETIME?
options: DATETIME is timezone-aware while TIMESTAMP is not
TIMESTAMP is timezone-aware (stored in UTC, converted on retrieval) and has a narrower range than DATETIME
TIMESTAMP and DATETIME are exact aliases with no functional difference
TIMESTAMP can only store dates, never times
questions.explain: MySQL's TIMESTAMP converts to/from UTC automatically and has a narrower supported range than DATETIME -- documented MySQL behavior.

questions.q: Which SQL Server type is the modern, higher-precision recommended timestamp type (vs. the legacy DATETIME)?
options: SMALLDATETIME
DATETIME2
TIMESTAMP
DATETIMEOFFSET
questions.explain: DATETIME2 is the modern, higher-precision timestamp type in SQL Server, recommended over the legacy DATETIME.

questions.q: What role does PostgreSQL's TIMESTAMPTZ play, and what SQL Server type is it comparable to?
options: A date-only type, comparable to SQL Server's DATE
A deprecated type no longer recommended in modern PostgreSQL
An approximate numeric type, unrelated to dates
A timezone-aware timestamp, comparable to SQL Server's DATETIMEOFFSET
questions.explain: TIMESTAMPTZ explicitly handles timezone information, filling a similar role to SQL Server's DATETIMEOFFSET.

questions.q: If you need a wide date range in MySQL with no automatic timezone conversion, which type should you choose?
options: DATETIME
TIMESTAMP
DATE
TIMESTAMPTZ
questions.explain: DATETIME offers a wider range than TIMESTAMP and does not perform the automatic UTC conversion that TIMESTAMP does.
